The languages are virtually identical in structure, though Kanum appears to differ somewhat from the other three in phonology. ... Vowel length is phonemic. new_statements.rule_in_words: No placement rule is given. Wurm's group-level characterisation of the Tonda Sub-Family (Tonda, Lower Morehead, Upper Morehead and Kanum, the last known to him only through Drabbe 1954 and Boelaars 1950) is that word stress exists, is 'fairly complex' and rhythmic, and that there is no tone. Nothing says which syllable is stressed, and nothing is said about Bädi in particular; Wurm's 'Kanum' is Drabbe's Yanggandur-Onggaya dialect (= Ngkolmpu, whose Onggaya variety is Baedi).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned beyond the phrase 'rhythm principles'.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Wurm adds that Kanum 'appears to differ somewhat from the other three in phonology' without specifying how.
new_statements.domain_note: Unspecified; a typological summary of a sub-family, not a word-level rule. The only Ngkolmpu descriptions (Carroll 2016, 2021) presuppose word-level stress but state no rule, and Evans 2021 (p. 7) says Southern New Guinea languages have 'no.. distinctive stress except for Urama'.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog's 'Ngkontar Baedi' badi1247 [khd] = Bädi / Baedi / Bedi Kanum. Carroll 2016 (pp. 2-3, 5-7) and Carroll 2021 (p. 33) treat Baedi/Bedi as the second, moribund dialect of Ngkolmpu (Ngkontar = Yanggandur, ngka1235 Ngkolmpu [kcd]; Baedi = Onggaya, ~6-10 elderly rememberers, no longer spoken); Glottolog instead splits them into two languages under Ngkantr, and its note on Donohue n.d. maps Tomer to khd and Onggaya to kcd, so the village-to-code assignment is inconsistent between sources. Everything descriptive (Carroll 2016, 2021; Donohue's Kanum page; SIL 2009 wordlists) is Ngkontar Ngkolmpu, not Bädi. Drabbe 1954's 'Kanum' (per Wurm 1971 p. 155: the dialect of 'Yenggalntyur and Onggaya', 165 speakers) covers the Ngkontar+Baedi unit; Wurm's stress sentence is about the whole Tonda Sub-Family.

sources.note: p. 33: 'There are two distinct dialects of Ngkolmpu: Ngkontar and Bedi.. Bedi is spoken in the coastal region near the contemporary village of Osnggaya [Onggaya]'; a 2017 visit found six elderly rememberers; 'The variety described in this paper is Ngkontar'. Sections: consonants, vowels, phonotactics, recorded passage; the words stress, accent, prosody, intonation do not occur in the article.

sources.citation: Carroll, Matthew J. 2016 [2017]. The Ngkolmpu Language with special reference to distributed exponence. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl 1885/116801).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: pp. 2-3, 5-7 (Table 1.1), 9: Ngkolmpu has two varieties, Ngkontar (Yanggandur, ~150 speakers) and Baedi (Onggaya, ~10, 'no longer a spoken language', 'only remembered by a handful of older people'); all data are Ngkontar. Ch. 2 Phonology has no stress/prosody section; stress is only presupposed (infinitive prefix 'always unstressed', topic clitic 'never attracts stress', noun+modifier = 'individual stress for each word'). Nothing on Baedi phonology.
